cards.front: Mitosis vs meiosis: number and ploidy of daughter cells?
cards.back: Mitosis: 2 diploid cells, genetically identical. Meiosis: 4 haploid cells, genetically different.

cards.text: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes happens in {{c1::prophase I}} of meiosis, at sites called {{c2::chiasmata}}.

cards.front: In which phase do **homologous chromosomes** separate?
cards.extra: Sister chromatids stay together until anaphase II.

cards.front: In which phases do **sister chromatids** separate?
cards.back: Anaphase of mitosis and anaphase II of meiosis.
Pairing of homologous chromosomes along their length in prophase I (via the synaptonemal complex)

cards.front: Two sources of genetic variation produced by meiosis itself?
cards.back: Crossing over (prophase I) and independent assortment of homologues (metaphase I).
cards.extra: Random fertilisation adds a third, but it is not part of meiosis.

cards.text: The {{c1::kinetochore}} is the protein complex on the centromere where spindle microtubules attach.

cards.front: What does the spindle assembly checkpoint control?
cards.back: The metaphase → anaphase transition: anaphase waits until every kinetochore is attached to the spindle.

cards.front: Which enzyme cleaves cohesin to start anaphase, and what activates it?
cards.back: Separase, activated when the APC/C triggers degradation of securin.

cards.front: Nondisjunction: what is it and one clinical consequence?
cards.back: Failure of chromosomes to separate correctly in meiosis I or II, giving aneuploid gametes; e.g. trisomy 21 (Down syndrome).

cards.front: Why is meiosis called a *reduction* division?
cards.back: Meiosis I halves the chromosome number (2n → n) by separating homologues; meiosis II then separates sister chromatids like mitosis.
